questions.question: How does the vigil mechanism or whistle-blower policy work: who can report, through which channel, and who receives the reports?
questions.answer: HDFC AMC's Whistle Blower Policy (approved 16 April 2018, last modified 15 October 2024) is made under s.177(9) of the Companies Act, LODR Reg. 22, MF Regulations Reg. 25 and PIT Regulations 9A(6) and 5H(5). Who can report: employees, directors and trustees, plus stakeholders such as investors and unit holders, shareholders, clients, vendors, distributors, brokers and service providers. What they can report: malpractice, actual or suspected fraud, breaches of the Code of Conduct or company policies, abuse of power, and leakage of AMC or HDFC MF unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI). How: by email, in person, by letter, or through a third-party web portal (www.cwiportal.com, organisation code HDFCAMC), which issues a tracking number and keeps the reporter's identity confidential. Who receives reports: a Whistleblower-Complaints Committee (Head of HR, CFO, Company Secretary). UPSI leaks go to a separate AMC UPSI Committee or HDFC MF UPSI Committee. Complaints against a director or the MD, cases where the reporter is dissatisfied, and UPSI leaks involving the CS/CO or CEO/MD can go directly to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee. Timelines: a preliminary inquiry starts within 7 working days, the investigation finishes within 8 weeks, and action is decided within 7 working days after that. Status reports go to the Audit Committee every half-year, and records are kept for at least 8 years. The FY26 annual report says no person was denied access to the Audit Committee.

questions.question: Which investor types does the AMC accept, restrict or subject to extra onboarding checks (NRIs, US/Canada persons, FPIs, trusts, other non-individuals)?
questions.answer: The mutual fund accepts resident individuals, NRIs, PIOs, OCIs and FPIs. NRIs, PIOs and OCIs pay on a repatriation basis from NRE/FCNR accounts or on a non-repatriation basis from NRO accounts. These investors may be asked for any further documents the AMC, Mutual Fund or Registrar requires. FPIs must hold DDP registration under the SEBI FPI Regulations. Non-individual applicants must file an Ultimate Beneficial Ownership declaration, and each UBO must be KYC compliant. All investors go through FATCA/CRS due diligence to identify foreign reportable accounts. Aadhaar eKYC is limited to resident individuals and is not available to NRIs, non-individuals or minors. PAN-exempt micro investments (PEKRN) are open only to individuals (including NRIs but not PIOs), minors and sole proprietary firms. The PMS disclosure document defines accredited and large value accredited investors, who get regulatory concessions, and defines clients to include individuals, HUFs, corporates, trusts and Indian or foreign institutional investors. No fetched source states whether US or Canada residents are accepted or restricted: the SAI text I could decode mentions the US only in the FATCA context.
